Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Sorrell
Analyst: JT Mathis
Date: 02/04/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 125 as introduced would prohibit a public official or public employee from advocating in favor of, or against, statewide and local ballot measures by such methods:
(1) Expending public funds;
(2) Presenting or distributing political literature; and
(3) Placement of a political poster on government property.
This bill could further increase receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, and local jails by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by this bill and the penalties imposed.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government

Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Sorrell
Analyst: JT Mathis
Date: 02/09/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 125 as amended and reported by the Committee on State Government would prohibit a public official or public employee from advocating in favor of, or against, statewide and local ballot measures by such methods:
(1) Expending public funds;
(2) Presenting or distributing political literature; and
(3) Placement of a political poster on government property.
This bill would also require a public official or public employee to repay any such funds expended contrary to the provisions of this bill.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government
